jp: 来月[らいげつ]の旅行[りょこう]の行[い]き先[さき]がやっと{決[き]まりました|tr-kimaru}。
en: The destination for next month's trip has finally been decided.
why: The destination is the subject (が) and nobody is named as deciding, so the intransitive 決まる is used.

jp: 旅行[りょこう]の日程[にってい]をみんなで{決[き]めました|tr-kimaru}。
en: We all decided the schedule of the trip together.
why: People act on the schedule (を), so the transitive 決める is needed.

jp: 大学[だいがく]を出[で]る前[まえ]に、就職先[しゅうしょくさき]が{決[き]まりました|tr-kimaru}。
en: Before I left university, my place of employment was settled.
why: The job placement came about as a result and is marked by が, so the intransitive 決まる is right.

jp: 結婚式[けっこんしき]の日[ひ]が{決[き]まったら|tr-kimaru}、教[おし]えてください。
en: Once the date of the wedding is decided, please let me know.
why: The date is the subject (が) of a state that will come about, so the intransitive 決まる is used.

jp: 先生[せんせい]、レポートのテーマを{決[き]めました|tr-kimaru}。
en: Teacher, I have decided my report topic.
why: The speaker chose the topic (を), so the transitive 決める is needed.

jp: 引[ひ]っ越[こ]しの日[ひ]がまだ{決[き]まっていません|tr-kimaru}。
en: The moving date has not been decided yet.
why: The date (が) is in a not-yet-settled state, which is the intransitive 決まる with まだ.

jp: 将来[しょうらい]の仕事[しごと]を早[はや]く{決[き]めたほうがいいですよ|tr-kimaru}。
en: You had better decide on your future job early.
d: 決[き]まったほうがいいですよ
決[き]まらないほうがいいですよ
決[き]めたくないですよ
why: The job is the object (を) that the listener must choose, so the transitive 決める fits the advice.

jp: 会議[かいぎ]の日時[にちじ]が{決[き]まりました|tr-kimaru}ので、メールで連絡[れんらく]します。
en: The date and time of the meeting have been decided, so I will let you know by e-mail.
why: が with a settled outcome and no one deciding in view takes 決まる, in the past because it is already settled.

jp: 部屋[へや]の色[いろ]を白[しろ]に{決[き]めました|tr-kimaru}。
en: I decided on white for the colour of my room.
why: The speaker made the choice (を), so the transitive 決める is used.

jp: 次[つぎ]の担当[たんとう]をじゃんけんで{決[き]めましょう|tr-kimaru}。
en: Let's decide who is in charge next by rock-paper-scissors.
why: An invitation to decide the next person in charge (を) needs the transitive 決める.

jp: 子[こ]どもたちの名前[なまえ]を、夫婦[ふうふ]で話[はな]し合[あ]って{決[き]めました|tr-kimaru}。
en: The couple talked it over and decided the children's names.
why: The couple carry out the decision, so the transitive 決める is used.

jp: 信号[しんごう]が赤[あか]から青[あお]に{変[か]わったら|tr-kimaru}、渡[わた]りましょう。
en: Let's cross when the light changes from red to green.
why: The light (が) changes by itself, so the intransitive 変わる; 変わらなければ would reverse the condition.

jp: 髪型[かみがた]を{変[か]えました|tr-kimaru}。
en: I changed my hairstyle.
why: Someone changes the hairstyle on purpose (を), so the transitive 変える is needed.

jp: 引[ひ]っ越[こ]してから、生活[せいかつ]が大[おお]きく{変[か]わりました|tr-kimaru}。
en: My life has changed a lot since I moved.
why: Life (が) changed as a result, with no agent in the sentence, so 変わる is used.

jp: 来週[らいしゅう]から、会議[かいぎ]の時間[じかん]を{変[か]えます|tr-kimaru}。
en: From next week we will change the time of the meeting.
why: Someone is making the change (を), so the transitive 変える; the future ending fits 来週から.

jp: 山[やま]の天気[てんき]は急[きゅう]に{変[か]わる|tr-kimaru}ことがあります。
en: The weather in the mountains can change suddenly.
why: The weather changes by itself (が), so 変わる; 変わらない would say it never changes.

jp: 店[みせ]の名前[なまえ]を{変[か]えるつもりです|tr-kimaru}。
en: I intend to change the name of my shop.
d: 変[か]えたことがあります
変[か]わったことがあります
why: The owner will change the name on purpose (を), and つもり states the intention.

jp: 駅[えき]の名前[なまえ]が来年[らいねん]から{変[か]わります|tr-kimaru}。
en: The name of the station will change from next year.
why: The name (が) is the thing that changes, and 来年から makes it future, so 変わります.

jp: 先生[せんせい]に言[い]われて、勉強[べんきょう]の方法[ほうほう]を{変[か]えました|tr-kimaru}。
en: My teacher told me to, so I changed my way of studying.
why: The learner deliberately changed the method (を), so the transitive 変える.

jp: 気分[きぶん]を{変[か]えるために|tr-kimaru}、散歩[さんぽ]に行[い]きました。
en: I went for a walk in order to change my mood.
why: The speaker acts on the mood (を) for a purpose, so 変える; the negative forms reverse the purpose.

jp: この町[まち]は、十年[じゅうねん]前[まえ]から少[すこ]しも{変[か]わっていません|tr-kimaru}。
en: This town has not changed at all in the last ten years.
why: The town itself stays unchanged and there is no object, so 変わる; 少しも needs a negative, so 変わっていません.

jp: 公園[こうえん]に子[こ]どもたちが{集[あつ]まっています|tr-kimaru}。
en: Children are gathered in the park.
why: The children (が) come together by themselves, so the intransitive 集まる.

jp: 趣味[しゅみ]で古[ふる]い切手[きって]を{集[あつ]めています|tr-kimaru}。
en: As a hobby I collect old stamps.
why: A person collects the stamps (を), so the transitive 集める.

jp: 日曜日[にちようび]の祭[まつ]りには、たくさんの人[ひと]が{集[あつ]まりました|tr-kimaru}。
en: Many people gathered at the festival on Sunday.
why: The crowd (が) came on their own, so 集まる, not the transitive 集める.

jp: 先生[せんせい]は生徒[せいと]のノートを{集[あつ]めました|tr-kimaru}。
en: The teacher collected the students' notebooks.
why: The teacher acts on the notebooks (を), so the transitive 集める.

jp: クラスのみんなが{集[あつ]まったら|tr-kimaru}、始[はじ]めましょう。
en: Let's begin once everyone in the class has gathered.
why: みんなが is the subject who come together, so the intransitive 集まったら.

jp: 会費[かいひ]を明日[あした]までに{集[あつ]めなければなりません|tr-kimaru}。
en: I have to collect the membership fees by tomorrow.
d: 集[あつ]まらなければなりません
集[あつ]めてはいけません
集[あつ]まってはいけません
why: Someone must collect the fees (を), so 集める; the other options reverse the obligation or lose the object.

jp: お祝[いわ]いのために、親戚[しんせき]が私[わたし]の家[いえ]に{集[あつ]まります|tr-kimaru}。
en: My relatives will gather at my house for the celebration.
why: The relatives (が) come together themselves, so 集まる; the future fits the plan.

jp: 駅[えき]の前[まえ]で、寄付[きふ]のお金[かね]を{集[あつ]めています|tr-kimaru}。
en: They are collecting donations in front of the station.
why: People gather the money actively (を), so the transitive 集める.

jp: 論文[ろんぶん]のために、図書館[としょかん]で資料[しりょう]を{集[あつ]めました|tr-kimaru}。
en: I collected materials at the library for my thesis.
why: The student gathers materials (を), so 集める; 集まる would mean they came together by themselves.

jp: なくした財布[さいふ]が{見[み]つかりました|tr-kimaru}。
en: My lost wallet has been found.
why: The wallet (が) turned up without anyone's search being in focus, so the intransitive 見つかる.

jp: 公園[こうえん]で小[ちい]さい猫[ねこ]を{見[み]つけました|tr-kimaru}。
en: I found a small cat in the park.
why: The speaker is the finder and the cat is the object (を), so the transitive 見つける.

jp: 探[さが]していた本[ほん]が、やっと{見[み]つかりました|tr-kimaru}。
en: The book I had been looking for was finally found.
why: The book (が) is what turned up, so 見つかる; 見つける would need を.

jp: かばんの中[なか]を探[さが]しても、鍵[かぎ]が{見[み]つかりません|tr-kimaru}。
en: Even when I look through my bag, I can't find my key.
why: The key (が) does not appear however I look, so the intransitive 見つかる in the negative.

jp: 安[やす]いホテルを{見[み]つけることができました|tr-kimaru}。
en: I was able to find a cheap hotel.
d: 見[み]つかることができました
見[み]つけられませんでした
見[み]つかりませんでした
why: The speaker finds the hotel (を), so 見つける; 見つかる cannot take を or ことができる.

jp: いい仕事[しごと]が{見[み]つかったら|tr-kimaru}、すぐに引[ひ]っ越[こ]します。
en: If a good job turns up, I will move right away.
d: 見[み]つからなかったら
why: The job (が) is what turns up, so 見つかる; 見つからなかったら would reverse the condition.

jp: 母[はは]は、私[わたし]が隠[かく]した日記[にっき]を{見[み]つけました|tr-kimaru}。
en: My mother found the diary that I had hidden.
d: 見[み]つけませんでした
why: The mother is the finder and the diary the object (を), so the transitive 見つける.

jp: 犯人[はんにん]がまだ{見[み]つかっていません|tr-kimaru}。
en: The culprit has not been found yet.
why: The culprit (が) has not turned up; まだ goes with a negative state, so 見つかっていません.

jp: 間違[まちが]いを{見[み]つけたら|tr-kimaru}、教[おし]えてください。
en: If you find a mistake, please tell me.
why: The listener finds the mistake (を), so 見つける; the other forms lose the object or reverse the condition.

jp: 子[こ]どもたちは森[もり]の中[なか]で珍[めずら]しい虫[むし]を{見[み]つけました|tr-kimaru}。
en: The children found a rare insect in the forest.
why: The children found it actively and the insect is the object (を), so 見つける.

jp: 私[わたし]の気持[きも]ちが彼[かれ]に{伝[つた]わりました|tr-kimaru}。
en: My feelings got across to him.
why: The feelings (が) reached him by themselves, so the intransitive 伝わる.

jp: 先生[せんせい]に私[わたし]の意見[いけん]を{伝[つた]えました|tr-kimaru}。
en: I told the teacher my opinion.
why: The speaker conveys the opinion (を), so the transitive 伝える.

jp: 地震[じしん]のニュースが、すぐに世界中[せかいじゅう]に{伝[つた]わりました|tr-kimaru}。
en: The news of the earthquake spread around the world immediately.
why: The news (が) travelled on its own, with no one conveying it in view, so 伝わる.

jp: 社長[しゃちょう]にこのメッセージを{伝[つた]えてください|tr-kimaru}。
en: Please pass this message on to the president.
d: 伝[つた]わってください
伝[つた]えないでください
伝[つた]わらないでください
why: A request to convey the message (を) needs the transitive 伝える; 伝わる cannot be requested.

jp: 先生[せんせい]の熱意[ねつい]が、生徒[せいと]たちに{伝[つた]わったようです|tr-kimaru}。
en: It seems the teacher's enthusiasm got across to the students.
d: 伝[つた]わらないようです
伝[つた]えないようです
why: The enthusiasm (が) reached the students by itself, so 伝わる; the negatives contradict the English.

jp: ありがとうの気持[きも]ちを、手紙[てがみ]で{伝[つた]えたいです|tr-kimaru}。
en: I want to convey my feelings of thanks in a letter.
d: 伝[つた]えたくないです
why: The writer wants to act on the feelings (を), so the transitive 伝える; 伝わりたい is not natural Japanese.

jp: 言葉[ことば]が通[つう]じなくても、笑顔[えがお]で気持[きも]ちが{伝[つた]わります|tr-kimaru}。
en: Even if the language doesn't get through, feelings come across with a smile.
why: The feelings (が) come across by themselves, so 伝わる; 伝わりません would deny the point.

jp: 会議[かいぎ]の時間[じかん]を山田[やまだ]さんに{伝[つた]えましたか|tr-kimaru}。
en: Did you tell Mr. Yamada the time of the meeting?
d: 伝[つた]わっていますか
why: The listener is asked whether they conveyed the time (を), so the transitive 伝える.

jp: この寺[てら]の昔話[むかしばなし]が、村[むら]に{伝[つた]わっています|tr-kimaru}。
en: The old tale of this temple has been handed down in the village.
why: The tale (が) has been passed down on its own, so 伝わっています; 伝える would need an agent and を.

jp: 難[むずか]しいことを子[こ]どもにわかりやすく{伝[つた]えるのは|tr-kimaru}大変[たいへん]です。
en: Conveying difficult things to children in an easy way is hard.
d: 伝[つた]えられないのは
why: Someone must do the conveying of the difficult matter (を), so 伝える; 伝わる lacks an agent.

jp: 駅[えき]の場所[ばしょ]を、外国人[がいこくじん]に英語[えいご]で{伝[つた]えました|tr-kimaru}。
en: I explained in English where the station is to a foreigner.
why: The speaker conveyed the location (を), so the transitive 伝える.

jp: ルールは、先[さき]にみんなで{決[き]めておきましょう|tr-kimaru}。
en: Let's decide the rules together beforehand.
d: 決[き]まっておきましょう
決[き]めたくありません
why: ルール is the object (は topic) being decided by people, so 決める; 決まっておく cannot work.

jp: 試合[しあい]の場所[ばしょ]が雨[あめ]のせいで{変[か]わりました|tr-kimaru}。
en: The venue of the match changed because of the rain.
why: The venue (が) changed because of the weather with no one in view acting, so the intransitive 変わる.

jp: クラスの旅行[りょこう]の写真[しゃしん]を、みんなから{集[あつ]めています|tr-kimaru}。
en: I am collecting photos of the class trip from everyone.
why: The speaker gathers the photos (を) from people, so the transitive 集める.

jp: 新[あたら]しい店長[てんちょう]が来月[らいげつ]の会議[かいぎ]で{決[き]まります|tr-kimaru}。
en: The new store manager will be decided at next month's meeting.
why: The manager (が) is the subject of the outcome, and 来月 makes it future, so 決まります.
